facts.claim: As at November 2026, Smartraveller's overall advice level for Greece is 'Exercise normal safety precautions' (still current at 11 November 2026, updated 30 September 2026); its latest update warns to take care swimming because of boat traffic, coastal hazards, strong currents and marine life, and to swim at patrolled beaches where possible.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says heatwaves are frequent in Greece over the summer months and can cause heat exhaustion, heat stroke and death; it advises drinking water, wearing a hat and light clothing and staying in air-conditioned buildings or shaded areas, and notes many major tourist sites have little shade.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says wildfires occur in Greece during the extended summer period, from June to September, including near cities and tourist locations, prompting evacuations; fires can start with little warning and travel quickly, so avoid affected areas and follow local authorities' advice.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'Getting married overseas' page (last updated 18/08/2026, re-checked 11 November 2026, unchanged from wedding-in-crete fact_119) says some countries ask you to prove you are free to marry, most commonly with a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and registry certificates; DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia but some local authorities only accept ones issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need one, where to get it, and whether it needs an authentication or apostille. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says (re-checked 11 November 2026, unchanged from wedding-in-crete fact_120) an overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia but in most cases is legally recognised if valid where it took place and valid under Australian law had it occurred here; a foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of marriage but may not work as proof of a name change. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, the Australian Embassy in Athens (re-checked 11 November 2026, unchanged from wedding-in-crete fact_121) lists among its notarial services witnessing application forms for, and issuing, Certificates of No Impediment (CNI), witnessing notices of intended marriage, and legalisation by authentication or apostille. All notarial services need an appointment (Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 12:30pm), though apostille and CNI documents can be submitted by post; legalised documents and CNIs are ready for collection within two working days unless same-day collection is arranged; the Embassy gives no legal advice, honorary consuls cannot provide notarial services, and fees apply. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

Akrotiri Beach Resort & Spa, Paleokastritsa, describes itself as a five-star adult-friendly resort and says guests can 'admire the breathtaking views from every corner of the resort', with Superior East Side rooms having 'an open sea view' and West Side rooms looking to 'the picturesque sunsets of Alipa harbor'. Its homepage and Experiences & Activities page do not mention weddings, and /weddings/ returns a 404 (checked 2026-11-11), so it fails the inclusion rule.

Hellenic National Meteorological Service climatic data for the Kerkyra (Corfu) station, data period 1955 to 2010: average maximum monthly temperature is 24.0°C in May, 28.2°C in June, 31.2°C in July, 31.5°C in August, 27.5°C in September and 23.2°C in October; average minimum is 13.3°C in May, 18.9°C in July, 19.3°C in August and 13.7°C in October.

Hellenic National Meteorological Service climatic data for Kerkyra (1955 to 2010): average monthly precipitation days are 7.7 in May, 4.8 in June, 3.3 in July, 3.3 in August, 7.4 in September and 11.4 in October (14.7 in November); average monthly rainfall is 36.5 mm in May, 15.5 mm in June, 8.7 mm in July, 21.7 mm in August, 87.8 mm in September and 140.4 mm in October.

Hellenic National Meteorological Service climatic data for Kerkyra (1955 to 2010): the prevailing wind is westerly in June, July and August and southerly in May, September and October; mean monthly relative humidity is about 62 percent in July and August, rising to 70.3 percent in September and 74.9 percent in October.

Corfu Airport (CFU) has an official website at cfu-airport.gr, which describes itself as 'The official website of Corfu Airport (CFU)' and links to 'The official Fraport Greece Magazine'; its To & From the Airport section lists getting there by GPS, by public bus ('Direct Bus Service To and From the airport') and by taxi. The site's detail pages on bus routes, journey times and the operator's formal name were not read in this batch.

insider_details.detail: Corfu's driest, hottest stretch is July and August, with only about 3 rain days a month but average highs above 31°C, and Smartraveller warns of frequent summer heatwaves and wildfires from June to September: plan shaded ceremony spots, a late-afternoon start and water stations, and keep an indoor or covered fallback.

For a cooler date with still-low rain, June (average high 28.2°C, 4.8 rain days) and September (27.5°C, 7.4 rain days) are the balance points; by October rain days climb to 11.4, so an outdoor-only plan needs a confirmed wet-weather space.

West-coast ceremonies in summer sit in Corfu's prevailing westerly wind (June to August), so ask the venue how exposed the ceremony and dinner spots are, and secure arbours, florals and candles accordingly.

If guests plan a pre-wedding swim, Smartraveller's latest Greece update flags boat traffic, strong currents and coastal hazards and suggests patrolled beaches, which is worth a line in the welcome pack.

Couples needing a CNI or apostille should book the Embassy in Athens early: appointments run Monday to Friday mornings only, documents take two working days, and there are no notarial services at honorary consulates, so build this into the paperwork timeline.
